title: Do Language Models Exhibit the Same Cognitive Biases in Problem Solving as Human Learners?

paper.authors: Andreas Opedal, Alessandro Stolfo, Haruki Shirakami, Ying Jiao, Ryan Cotterell, Bernhard Schoelkopf, Abulhair Saparov, Mrinmaya Sachan
paper.venue: Forty-first International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2024); arXiv v1 2024-01-31, v2 2024-06-17

dependence.note: The LLMs are the objects of study (do they show child-like biases). Test problems are synthetic pairs generated by a neuro-symbolic pipeline (with a GPT-3.5-turbo paraphrase/correction step) and are shipped as CSVs, so no regeneration is needed.

claim.statement: With zero-shot chain-of-thought prompting, GPT-4 Turbo exhibits a consistency bias - 90.4% accuracy on consistent vs 72.4% on inconsistent comparison problems (CATE 18.0 points, paired t-test p < 0.001, 500 problem pairs) - and a transfer-vs-comparison bias (99.2% vs 91.4%, CATE 7.8, p < 0.001), but no carry effect (99.6% vs 99.6%, CATE 0.0) - Table 2, CoT rows.
claim.metric: accuracy (exact match of the first extracted number vs gold answer) per condition; CATE = acc(easy condition) - acc(hard condition) over paired problems; two-tailed paired t-test, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR at alpha = 0.05 per bias family

original_values.direct_prompting: GPT-4 Turbo not reported in Table 2 (only GPT-3.5 Turbo has a direct row)

claim.original_source: Table 2 (page 7) and Table 5 (Appendix B.3) of arXiv 2401.18070

protocol.model: GPT-4 Turbo (snapshot not stated; eval.py takes the model string from a Hydra config whose default is null)
protocol.model_status: UNRESOLVED / presumed DEAD: experiments predate arXiv v1 (2024-01-31), so the arm must have been gpt-4-1106-preview or gpt-4-0125-preview (both shut down 2026-03-26). gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 (dying) was released after v1 and can only serve as a sibling snapshot unless the ICML camera-ready (v2, June 2024) re-ran the experiments.
protocol.prompt_source: evaluation/eval.py (direct_inference, cot_inference); Section 5.1 of the paper

messages.direct: [system (gpt-4 only): 'Answer the following questions with a single numerical value, do not output any additional text.'] user: '{problem}\nThe answer (Arabic numerals) is ' (instruction-tuned pattern; base-model pattern 'Q: {problem}\nA: The answer (arabic numerals) is ')
messages.cot_step1: user: 'Q: {problem}\nA: Let's think step by step. '  (max_tokens 256)
messages.cot_step2: user: '{step1 output}\nTherefore, the answer (arabic numerals) is '  (max_tokens 16); answer = first number in the output

protocol.n_items: 3 tests x 500 problem pairs = 1,500 pairs = 3,000 problems (data/cons_500.csv, comp_trans_500.csv, carry_500.csv)
protocol.evaluation: Automatic: extract the first number, exact match vs the 'answer' column; CATE and paired t-test in eval.py (scipy ttest_rel); BH correction across the tests of one bias family.
protocol.environment_check: Dry-run eval.py's parsing on the released CSVs; confirm the CoT two-stage format and number extraction (commas/periods stripped) before spending.

artifacts.data_path: external/repos/W4391463123/eth-lre__solving-biases/data/cons_500.csv, comp_trans_500.csv, carry_500.csv (public, in repo; columns: question, consistent/inconsistent bodies, paraphrases, answer)
artifacts.notes: Model outputs (eval_out/) are not in the repo; the generation pipeline (concate_temp/) is included but not needed for re-execution.

blockers: original GPT-4 Turbo snapshot unpinned and, by date, dead (gpt-4-1106-preview / gpt-4-0125-preview); the 'gpt-4-turbo' census hit is alias-only
no license on data/code - redistribution of the problems in our archive needs author consent
near-ceiling accuracies (99%+) make the carry test uninformative for strong models

baseline_alive.note: none - optional sibling arm gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 (P3 successor-family), labelled as sibling

successors: claude (current Anthropic flagship, dated snapshot fixed at run time)
gemini (current Google flagship, dated snapshot fixed at run time)
llama (open weights, e.g. Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, weights hash fixed)
qwen (open weights, e.g. Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct, weights hash fixed)

budget.assumptions: CoT protocol: 2 calls per problem x 3,000 problems = 6,000 calls per seed x 3 seeds; step 1 ~120 in / ~180 out (cap 256), step 2 ~300 in / ~10 out. Greedy decoding -> 1 seed (~$30) would be defensible; direct-prompting rows would add 3,000 cheap calls per seed (~$5).

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1 on the three CoT CATEs: survival if consistency CATE > 0 with p < 0.05 and of the same order of magnitude (>= ~10 points), transfer-vs-comparison CATE > 0 with p < 0.05, and carry CATE ~ 0 (non-significant); partial if the directions hold but consistency significance is lost or the CATE shrinks below ~5 points; death if consistency CATE <= 0 or a significant positive carry effect appears.
judgment.notes: Ceiling effects: if a successor scores ~100% in both conditions the bias becomes unmeasurable - record as 'not judgeable (ceiling)' rather than death.

user_checks: Approve a sibling-snapshot arm with gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 (dying) in place of the dead Jan-2024 preview snapshot? (~$30 for 1 seed, ~$89 for 3)
Confirm choosing the CoT rows of Table 2 as the core claim (GPT-4 Turbo has no direct-prompting row).
Ask the authors (eth-lre) which snapshot 'GPT-4 Turbo' was and whether the camera-ready re-ran it.
domain_notes: Problems are synthetic arithmetic word problems built from MathWorld-style logical forms with a GPT-3.5-turbo linguistic-correction step already materialised in the CSVs; the human comparison is qualitative (child-learner literature) except for the 8-pair Hegarty et al. (1995) set. CATEs are paired differences on otherwise identical problem pairs, so they are robust to overall ability shifts but vulnerable to ceiling effects in newer models.
